# B2 — Process Lifecycle Hardening (design, revision 35)

Korean translation: [process-lifecycle-hardening_ko.md](process-lifecycle-hardening_ko.md)

> **Status: design proposal, not approved, not implemented.** This is revision 35. Earlier revisions were reviewed by the author and by independent reviewers; the finding counts and the inline labels used in the text (m1, MA-1, C-1 …) refer to those review reports. They are reports, not repository-reproducible facts, and they are **not** part of the current approval basis, which is the text of this document alone; no revision has been approved. **Revision 35 changes** (revision 35 has **not** been independently reviewed and **nothing here is approved**; > **Approval boundary (proposed).** *Windows only:* process-tree tracking, the Job Object, suspended spawn, `ResumeThread`, the Windows tree proof, `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` and the tracked-command capability of a Windows host. *Windows and POSIX common code (in the approval request):* the cancellation-safe settlement of untracked commands, the bounded pump drain, the fix of the `on_started`-exception leak, the common result and error contract and the regression protection of the provider CLIs. *POSIX contract (in scope as a design and code change):* an existing Workflow Task and TESTER step degrade to `UNTRACKED_PLATFORM`; a TEST_ONLY / Test Run request is refused before creation with `409 PROCESS_TRACKING_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`; a POSIX Runner publishes no tracking-capability row; an API-only instance judges by its local OS. In one sentence: the tracking feature is proposed for approval on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is **not** approved (§5.2 needs a handshake design and real-environment verification first); POSIX real-execution verification has **not** been done. Anything not verified is marked **(unverified)**. **Approval boundary (proposed; nothing is approved):** tracking on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is not approved; POSIX real-execution verification has not been done; root process exit detected first by `returncode`; as a result the normal-exit outcome of untracked commands can differ from today's TIMEOUT or ALREADY_EXITED.

## 1. Purpose and non-goals

Purpose: a command started through `CommandExecutor` is owned **as a tree**, not only as a root process. On natural exit, timeout, cancellation, Runner stop, coroutine cancellation and API/Runner crash, the tree is terminated, and **termination is reported as success only when it is proven**. When it cannot be proven the result is explicit (`TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED`), the caller keeps project ownership and the run is handed to the existing RECOVERY path.

Non-goals: containers, cgroups-as-a-requirement, worktrees, changing provider CLI behaviour, changing the Human Gate model, changing D5/D6/F decisions, any change to what a test command is allowed to run, any POSIX process-tracking implementation (§5.2; the POSIX degrade and refusal contract and the common untracked settlement hardening are in scope, see the approval boundary of the header). **Approval boundary (proposed; nothing is approved):** tracking on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is not approved; POSIX real-execution verification has not been done; root process exit detected first by `returncode`; as a result the normal-exit outcome of untracked commands can differ from today's TIMEOUT or ALREADY_EXITED.

## 2. Verified current state

| Area | Fact (file) |
|---|---|
| Spawn | `CommandExecutor._execute` (`app/infra/command_executor.py`): Windows `creationflags=CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`, POSIX `start_new_session=True`. No Job Object, no `killpg`. |
| Identity | `capture_identity(pid)` (`app/infra/process_control.py`) returns `ProcessIdentity(pid, create_time)` or `None` (process already gone, `AccessDenied`). |
| `on_started` | `await on_started(identity)` is called unguarded right after spawn, with no timeout. If the callback raises, `_execute` exits with the process running and no pump/waiter cleanup. |
| Natural exit | The 0.5 s loop breaks when `waiter = asyncio.create_task(proc.wait())` completes. `outcome is None` → **no termination call**, `CommandResult.termination` is `None`. Then `await asyncio.gather(*pumps)` waits for **pipe EOF without any bound**. **`proc.wait()` is not a usable root-exit signal here:** it completes only when the transport's connection is lost, i.e. after the pipes reached EOF (probe, §2.1). A descendant that inherited stdout/stderr and outlives the root therefore keeps `waiter` pending; the loop keeps running, evaluates `timeout_seconds` against a root that already exited and reports `outcome=TIMEOUT`, `exit_code=0`, `termination=ALREADY_EXITED` (reproduced twice, returning only when the descendant ended: 12.1 s and 10.1 s with `timeout_seconds=3`); because root-only termination does not kill the descendant, `gather(*pumps)` after the loop then waits for the descendant's whole lifetime. The descendant is never looked at. The same applies to every untracked command. |
| Root exit vs. pipe EOF | `proc.returncode` is set as soon as the root exits (about 0.1 s in the probe) **even while a grandchild holds the pipes**; only `wait()` (when started before the exit) and the pump tasks wait for EOF. Root exit is therefore observable from `returncode` independently of the pipes, never from `wait()`. |
| Termination | `_terminate` → `terminate_tree(identity, grace)` (`process_control.py`): returns early without killing when `check_alive` is not `STILL_ALIVE` (`ALREADY_EXITED`, `IDENTITY_MISMATCH`, `ACCESS_DENIED`, `UNKNOWN`); descendants are collected with `psutil.Process.children(recursive=True)` **from a still-live root only**; `terminate()` then `kill()` after the grace period; result `TERMINATED` / `ACCESS_DENIED` / `STILL_ALIVE`. If `identity is None` the executor falls back to `proc.kill()` and reports `KILLED_BY_HANDLE` (root only). A root that exits just before the timeout decision is reported as `outcome=TIMEOUT` with `termination=ALREADY_EXITED` (reviewer probe). |
| Cancellation | `run()` and `_execute()` only use `finally` to cancel `cancel_waiter` and release the slot. A `CancelledError` raised while the command runs propagates with the child alive, the pump/wait tasks pending and `_cancel_events[run_key]` not removed. |
| Existing helper name | `CommandExecutor._settle(acquire, waiter)` already exists (slot wait helper) and tests monkeypatch it (`tests/unit/test_command_executor.py`). The process settlement of §9 therefore needs a **different name** (`_settle_process`); `_settle` and `_acquire_slot` stay untouched. |
| Cooperative cancel | `CommandExecutor.cancel(run_key)` sets the events whose key is `run_key` or starts with `run_key + ":"`. Providers and `TestPolicyService` share **one** executor (`app/container.py`). `Runner._cancel_cli(run_id)` calls `provider.cancel(str(run_id))` → `executor.cancel(run_id)`; it is used by Runner stop and lease loss. **User cancel** reaches a command only through `StepRunner._watch_cancel(task_id, provider, run_key)`, which runs **only around the provider call** and is cancelled in `finally` (`step_runner.py:162-196`). Test commands get no `run_key`, no `on_started` and are not under any watcher: `TestPolicyService.run` builds `CommandSpec(...)` per command in a loop (`test_policy_service.py:138-142`), so between two commands of one policy no event is registered at all. |
| Open-test-command scope | Besides `run`, `TestPolicyService.collect_ids` (`python -m pytest --collect-only`) executes project code (conftest import) through the same executor, untracked. `ProjectService` runs `git clone` through it too and relies on `termination != "KILLED_BY_HANDLE"` (`project_service.py:110-117`). |
| Records | `Execution` (`app/models/tables.py`) has `pid`, `process_create_time`, `runner_id`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `terminated_at`, `outcome`, `detail` (JSONB). There is **no** column for process group / Job identity or termination status (the executor's `termination` string lands in `detail.termination`). `unterminated_executions` filters on **`finished_at IS NULL`** (`task_repository.py:156-159`). |
| Existing "unconfirmed" chain | Agent CLIs: `StepRunner._record_finish` leaves `finished_at` NULL when the outcome is TIMEOUT/IDLE/CANCELLED and the termination is not in `CONFIRMED_GONE ∪ {KILLED_BY_HANDLE}`, then raises `TerminationUnconfirmed` (`step_runner.py:215-246`); `WorkflowService` catches it and calls `_park_for_recovery` (`workflow_service.py:157-158`) → RECOVERY gate, Task not terminal, project ownership retained. A normal finish writes `finished_at`; a lost lease goes through `_discard_result`, which also writes `finished_at`. |
| STARTING-before-spawn | Exists only for agent CLIs: `StepRunner._record_start` commits `Execution(outcome=STARTING)` before the provider spawns; `on_started` writes `pid`/`process_create_time`. The orchestrator's authoritative test run writes its `Execution` row (role `TESTER`, provider `LOCAL`, `detail.orchestrator_test_run`) only **after** the run (`WorkflowService._do_test`). |
| Takeover | `LeaseService.acquire` finds unterminated executions of the expired run, terminates each by `(pid, create_time)` outside any transaction, and writes `finished_at` for those proven gone (`lease_service.py:102-131`). Root-only: `ALREADY_EXITED` ∈ `CONFIRMED_GONE`. A row without identity (`STARTING` without pid) or any result outside `CONFIRMED_GONE` → `AcquireStatus.UNCERTAIN` → `Runner._park_uncertain` opens a RECOVERY gate. |

### 2.1 Feasibility probes (Windows, this host)

Throw-away scripts outside the repository (scratchpad, not committed), **Windows 11, Python 3.14.6, psutil 7.2.2**:

- `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(..., creationflags=CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_SUSPENDED)` works; the Popen handle was reached through `proc._transport._proc._handle` (private attribute; the public `OpenProcess(pid)` route is covered by the last bullet).
- `ctypes` calls to `CreateJobObjectW`, `SetInformationJobObject(JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE)`, `AssignProcessToJobObject` succeeded for the suspended process, including for `.exe`, `.cmd` shim and `cmd` children, and **when the Runner itself runs inside another job (Claude Code's)** (nested assignment succeeded).
- A root that started a grandchild and great-grandchild showed **6 active processes** in `JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation.ActiveProcesses` in the author's probe (the venv `python.exe` shim re-executes); the last independent probe used a possibly wrong ctypes structure and could not reproduce the count, so **the exact count is unverified** — what the design relies on is only "greater than 0 while descendants live, 0 after `TerminateJobObject`", observed by the author and the first independent review. Descendants are inherited by the job and stay in it after the root exits.
- `TerminateJobObject` brought `ActiveProcesses` to **0** immediately; `QueryInformationJobObject` is usable as a *proof of an empty tree*.
- Killing the owner process ended the whole tree through `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`; observed only **1.5 s after** the kill (no longer-term or higher-load observation).
- A `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` request was **accepted without error** (nested environment) and the child **stayed in the job**.
- **Resume (revision 2):** with the process still suspended, `psutil.Process(pid).threads()` returned exactly one thread; `OpenThread(THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME)` + `ResumeThread` returned previous suspend count **1** and the process ran. `psutil.Process.resume()` also worked, but it is, to my knowledge, a wrapper over the same undocumented `NtResumeProcess` (**unverified**) and is not used.
- **Root exit vs. pipes (revision 3, corrected):** with a grandchild holding the inherited pipes, `proc.returncode` was set about 0.1 s after the root exited, and a `proc.wait()` awaited **after** that returned immediately; but the executor creates `asyncio.create_task(proc.wait())` **before** the exit, and that task did not complete until the pipes reached EOF (independent review: `wait_done` at 6.6 s, venv shim and base python alike). The stdout pipe stayed open (2 s observed) until `TerminateJobObject`, then reached EOF immediately. Revision 2's statement that `wait()` completes promptly was wrong.
- **Threads and handles (independent review, revision 3):** for the venv `python.exe`, a `.cmd` shim and `cmd /c`, a `CREATE_SUSPENDED` child always had exactly one thread (60/60 repetitions), `ResumeThread` returned previous count 1 every time, and `AssignProcessToJobObject` also worked with a handle from the public `OpenProcess(SET_QUOTA|TERMINATE|QUERY)` (no private attribute needed). `py.exe` launcher: not present, **unverified**.

Not verified: a real `gradle`/`mvn`/`mvnd`; restrictive outer jobs, Windows service execution, non-admin accounts, Windows versions older than 11; behaviour under other event loops; whether `conhost.exe` is a transient job member when no console exists; handle non-inheritance by grandchildren (§5.1 step 1 turns it into a test); **`JOB_CLOSE_SETTLE_SECONDS = 2.0` is an unverified design default, not a measurement** (the only observation is the limited probe that saw the tree gone 1.5 s after a kill on this host; other Windows environments, load and teardown speed are unverified); **POSIX anything**.

## 3. Invariants

Scope of I1–I4: **Windows tracked commands** (proposed approval scope). POSIX needs its own design (§5.2). **Approval boundary (proposed; nothing is approved):** tracking on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is not approved; POSIX real-execution verification has not been done; root process exit detected first by `returncode`; as a result the normal-exit outcome of untracked commands can differ from today's TIMEOUT or ALREADY_EXITED.

- **I1** Every process started by `CommandExecutor` for a *tracked* command belongs to exactly one Job Object created before the command can run user code.
- **I2** A tracked command's end is reported as `EXITED` or `TERMINATED` only when the Job is **proven empty** (`ActiveProcesses == 0`, confirmed by polling after the kill). Otherwise the result is `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED`.
- **I3** Cleanup is idempotent and shielded from cancellation: cancel, timeout, idle and Runner stop may all fire; the Job is terminated once, every caller observes the same final result, and a returning or raising run has always settled the tree first.
- **I4** The command is resumed only **after** its identity has been persisted. A tracked `Execution` row with `pid IS NULL` therefore proves that user code never ran; a spawn failure is distinguishable from "spawned, identity unknown".
- **I5** Nothing turns an unproven termination into a clean ownership release — **including a user abort.** `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` is delivered to the caller as the existing `TerminationUnconfirmed` error (§7.2); the project ownership stays and there is no automatic retry. A terminal transition of a Task with an open tracked execution (§7.4) never releases CLEAN: it ends `DIRTY_UNRESOLVED`. A user abort ends the Task; it does not replace the termination proof. The only exception is the explicit operator risk acceptance of §7.5, which is recorded as an exception, never as proof.
- **I6** Exactly two code paths release a project write lock (`release_on_terminal` and the crash reconciliation), and both apply the same unresolved-or-anomalous-execution rule through one common project-wide entry point (§7.4), and the write-owner acquisition applies it before a new owner is set (§7.4, acquisition guard); an architecture test forbids any third caller of `ProjectRepository.release`, and a second one pins every writer of `workspace_state='CLEAN'` (§7.4): the repository methods `release`, `accept_baseline` and `set_owner`, the initial INSERT of `ProjectService.create` as the single creation exception, and an allow-list of keys for `update_fields`.

## 4. States and results

Command lifecycle (one `CommandResult` per command; persisted where §6 says):

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `NOT_STARTED` | no spawn attempted (cancel before slot or before spawn; validation failure) |
| `STARTING` | spawn requested; Job created; process exists suspended or is about to |
| `RUNNING` | process spawned, assigned to its Job, identity persisted, resumed |
| `EXITED` | root exited by itself **and** the Job is proven empty (no survivors, or survivors terminated first → see `survivors`) |
| `CANCEL_REQUESTED` | cancel/timeout/idle/stop decided, termination not yet started |
| `TERMINATING` | kill sequence running |
| `TERMINATED` | killed by the executor and the Job is proven empty |
| `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` | a pid was obtained and the process was resumed, but Job emptiness could not be proven (access denied, still active after the kill and the poll deadline, Job handle lost or failed to query, identity mismatch). An unsupported platform is refused **before** spawn (§5.2, §6.2) and Job assignment happens while the process is still suspended (§5.1), so neither can end in this state |
| `SPAWN_FAILED` | **user code never ran**: executable not found, `OSError`, validation, identity unavailable or not persisted, or Job creation/assignment/resume failed **while the process was suspended and it was killed and proven gone** |

Rules:

- pid not obtained, or process killed while still suspended → `SPAWN_FAILED` (deterministic; the caller closes the `Execution` row and the project is released normally).
- pid obtained, process has run, emptiness not proven → `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED`.
- A root exit code is delivered together with the state; a non-zero exit is `EXITED` with `outcome=ERROR`, not a lifecycle failure. A root that exits before the timeout/idle decision is a **natural exit** (outcome from its exit code, never `TIMEOUT`).
- `TerminateJobObject` uses one fixed non-zero exit code (`JOB_TERMINATE_EXIT_CODE`, `policies.py`, value and validation in §9.3). Consumers rely on `outcome`/`lifecycle`, never on a job-killed root's exit code. That code is visible in `TestRunResult.exit_codes` and in the `exit_code=next((c for c in result.exit_codes if c), 0)` of the TESTER `Execution` (`workflow_service.py:778`; the first non-zero code, and **0** when no code is non-zero) for executor-terminated runs; it is documented as not meaningful unless `outcome` is SUCCESS/ERROR, and a test pins it.

`CommandResult` keeps `outcome: CliOutcome` and **adds** `lifecycle: ProcessLifecycle`, `tree: TreeProof` (`EMPTY | NOT_EMPTY | UNKNOWN` — `NOT_STARTED` is a lifecycle, not a tree value; **descriptive only**: no release rule reads it, they read `detail.proof`, §6.1; a process that never ran has `tree=EMPTY`), `spawn_failed: bool`, `survivors: bool` (descendants outlived the root and were terminated) and `reason: str | None` (codes such as `JOB_ASSIGN_FAILED`, kept in `detail`, never in `termination`).

### 4.1 Compatibility of `termination` strings

`termination: str | None` keeps today's vocabulary and meaning; B2 adds fields, it does not add or rename values.

| Situation | `lifecycle` | `termination` (unchanged vocabulary) |
|---|---|---|
| natural exit, Job empty | `EXITED` | `None` (as today) |
| natural exit, survivors terminated, Job empty | `EXITED` + `survivors=true` | `TERMINATED`; `outcome` stays SUCCESS/ERROR from the root exit |
| timeout / idle / cancel, Job emptied | `TERMINATED` | `TERMINATED` |
| Job still active after kill + poll deadline | `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` | `STILL_ALIVE` |
| terminate or query denied | `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` | `ACCESS_DENIED` |
| Job handle lost, query failed, identity mismatch | `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` | `UNKNOWN` |
| spawn failed / killed while suspended | `SPAWN_FAILED` | `None` |
| untracked command, no identity (today's fallback) | unchanged | `KILLED_BY_HANDLE` |
| untracked command, root gone before terminate (today) | unchanged | `ALREADY_EXITED` |

`StepRunner._confirmed_gone`, the `ProjectService` clone check, `LeaseService` and the string-pinning tests keep working without change. A golden test pins this table.

## 5. Platform ownership

### 5.1 Windows — Job Object (proposed approval scope)

**Approval boundary (proposed; nothing is approved):** tracking on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is not approved; POSIX real-execution verification has not been done; root process exit detected first by `returncode`; as a result the normal-exit outcome of untracked commands can differ from today's TIMEOUT or ALREADY_EXITED.

1. Create an anonymous Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` (`ctypes`, kernel32; no new dependency). The handle is created **non-inheritable**, without `BREAKAWAY_OK`/`SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK`. A test must prove that a grandchild does not inherit the handle (otherwise `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` would not fire when the Runner dies).
2. Spawn with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_SUSPENDED` so no user code runs before assignment.
3. `AssignProcessToJobObject`. On failure → kill the suspended process, prove it gone, `SPAWN_FAILED(JOB_ASSIGN_FAILED)`. Fail closed: a tracked command never runs without a Job. Nested jobs are allowed on current Windows (probed); the usual cause of `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` is insufficient handle access rights or an unusual outer job, not "nesting is forbidden".
4. `capture_identity(pid)`. `None` → kill, `SPAWN_FAILED(IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE)`.
5. Persist the identity through `on_started` **before resume**, bounded by `TRACKED_IDENTITY_PERSIST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (`policies.py`). The callback is **fenced** (§7.1): its transaction locks the Task, verifies the lease and updates the row only `WHERE finished_at IS NULL`; a lost lease or `rowcount == 0` means the row was already closed (for example by a takeover). Exception, timeout, cancellation or fence failure here → kill the still-suspended process, prove the Job empty, `SPAWN_FAILED(IDENTITY_PERSIST_FAILED)` (`IDENTITY_FENCED` for a fence failure); the command is not run. (Fixes the unguarded callback for tracked commands.)
6. **Resume with `ResumeThread` (decision H6):** locate the primary thread of the suspended process (`psutil.Process(pid).threads()` was probed; a Toolhelp32 snapshot is the documented alternative, **not probed**), require **exactly one** thread, `OpenThread(THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME)`, `ResumeThread`, require previous suspend count `== 1`. Any deviation → kill, `SPAWN_FAILED(RESUME_FAILED)`. `NtResumeProcess` and `psutil.Process.resume()` are **not** used. The timeout clock starts at resume, not at spawn.
7. **Startup self-test:** at Runner start, run the whole protocol once with a trivial child (spawn suspended → assign → resume by thread → terminate → `ActiveProcesses == 0`). The outcome is published as the process-tracking capability (§6.2): success → `SUPPORTED`; failure → `UNAVAILABLE` (`PROCESS_TRACKING_UNAVAILABLE`, tracked commands fail closed) and the `PROCESS_TRACKING` diagnostics item reports it. It covers the environment, not each future command.
8. Termination: `TerminateJobObject` (fixed exit code) then poll `QueryInformationJobObject(ActiveProcesses)` until 0 or `PROCESS_TERMINATE_GRACE_SECONDS`. A single non-zero value is never a verdict; `0` → `TERMINATED`, still non-zero at the deadline → `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED`.
9. **Natural exit (blocker fix, revision 3):** the root's exit is detected from **`proc.returncode is not None`** (polled on every 0.5 s tick, or `WaitForSingleObject` on the process handle), evaluated **before** the timeout/idle checks of the same tick, so a root that exited is a natural exit and is never reported as `TIMEOUT`; `proc.wait()` is **not** used as the signal (§2). Read the `returncode` **first**, then query `ActiveProcesses` (re-polled for `TREE_SETTLE_POLL_SECONDS` so a transient helper such as `conhost.exe` is not mistaken for a survivor). If it stays `> 0`: `TerminateJobObject` **before any pipe drain**, poll to 0, then drain pumps (§9). `0` → `EXITED`; survivors terminated → `EXITED` + `survivors=true` + `termination=TERMINATED`; not emptied → `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED`.
10. Runner/API crash: the Job handle dies with the process and `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` ends the tree. **This is a property of the OS handle; it is never stored and is used by recovery only under the conditions of §8.**
11. The Job handle is closed after the Job is proven empty. On `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` it is **retained** in the Runner's in-memory registry (§7.3) so that a later check or process exit still reaches the tree; a handle that cannot be closed is logged.

Limits stated honestly: a process that can ask for breakaway is not prevented from asking (the request was accepted in the probe) but stayed in the job; the job is created without breakaway flags. A launcher that starts work through another service or scheduled task is outside the job by construction. A narrow window exists between `CreateProcess` and `AssignProcessToJobObject` in which the Runner could die and leave a **suspended** orphan; no user code runs in it (recorded as `reason=SUSPENDED_ORPHAN_POSSIBLE` when recovery closes a pid-less row).

### 5.2 POSIX — session and process group (NOT APPROVED, unverified on this host)

Revision 1 of this section contained claims that cannot be kept. Findings that must be resolved **before** POSIX tracked commands may be approved:

- **No suspended spawn exists.** `start_new_session=True` runs the child immediately, so "pid persisted before user code" (I4) and "pid NULL ⇒ never ran" do **not** hold on POSIX. A handshake is required, for example a launcher that blocks on an extra pipe (`pass_fds`) until the parent has persisted the identity and sends a go byte, then `exec`s the real argv. Its design and failure modes are open.
- **Group id reuse.** A process group id can be reused after the group empties; a `killpg`/sweep keyed on a stored pgid/sid can hit an unrelated group or report a false `NOT_EMPTY`. The proof must not signal on a stored id alone.
- **Enumeration.** `psutil` provides no pgid/sid accessor; the enumeration source (`/proc`, `ps`, `os.getpgid`) and its zombie semantics must be specified. `process_group_id` is redundant under `start_new_session=True` (`pgid == sid == pid`).
- `setsid()`/double-fork escapes remain a known limitation (cgroup v2 `cgroup.kill` is a later option).

Until then, **POSIX tracked commands are not offered and not approved**:

- The orchestrator's existing TESTER-step test runs and `collect_ids` on POSIX **degrade to untracked execution** (today's behaviour: `start_new_session=True`, root-and-descendants `terminate_tree`), labelled `detail.tracking="UNTRACKED_PLATFORM"`. No `detail.tracked` marker is written, so none of the tracked rules of §7–§8 apply, and no tree guarantee is claimed.
- Anything that **requires** the tracked guarantee (the test-only Task of D4/E) is refused at the API boundary, before any Task row exists, with `409 PROCESS_TRACKING_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` (§6.2); the same code is the `PROCESS_TRACKING` diagnostics `cause`. E is therefore Windows-only until §5.2 is approved. The existing TESTER step keeps the degrade contract and, on POSIX, **writes no STARTING row** (the `Execution` row of the authoritative test run is written after the run, as today).
- This is deliberately different from a *Windows host whose self-test fails* (§5.1 step 7): that host is expected to support tracking, so silent degradation would hide a restriction and tracked commands fail closed instead (H5, code `PROCESS_TRACKING_UNAVAILABLE`, a different code from the POSIX one).
- The bounded pump drain of §9 and the root-exit detection by `returncode` use the same asyncio code on POSIX; their POSIX behaviour is read from code only and is **unverified**. Any real-environment POSIX test is listed as **not run**.
- **Approval boundary of this section (C6):** the POSIX **degrade and refusal contract** of the approval boundary of the header (the existing Workflow Task and TESTER step run as `UNTRACKED_PLATFORM`; a TEST_ONLY / Test Run request is refused before creation with `409 PROCESS_TRACKING_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`; a POSIX Runner publishes no capability row; an API-only instance judges by its local OS) is **in scope** as a design and code change; **POSIX process tracking is not approved** and **POSIX real-execution verification has not been done**. **Approval boundary (proposed; nothing is approved):** tracking on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is not approved; POSIX real-execution verification has not been done; root process exit detected first by `returncode`; as a result the normal-exit outcome of untracked commands can differ from today's TIMEOUT or ALREADY_EXITED.

## 6. Persistence

Decision H2: **no new column for execution facts.** The qualifier matters: it concerns execution facts only and does not forbid migration `0005`, which adds the two tables `runtime_capabilities` (§6.2) and `process_risk_requests` (§7.5) plus three additive partial indexes (§7.4, §7.5 items 4 and 11) and nothing else. `detail` (JSONB) carries the execution facts; `unterminated_executions` already filters on `finished_at`, and a pgid column would be redundant.

| Field | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pid`, `process_create_time` | `executions` (exist) | takeover and recovery identity; written by `on_started` before resume |
| `runner_id`, `run_id` | `executions` (exist) | which Runner incarnation / lease run owned the Job; the STARTING row **must** carry `run_id` (takeover selects `e.run_id == current.id`) |
| `started_at`, `terminated_at`, `finished_at` | `executions` (exist) | timing; `finished_at` marks a row as closed, but a closed row is only **proven** with a positive `detail.proof` (§6.1) |
| `detail.tracked = true`, `detail.v = 1` | `detail` | written in the STARTING commit, **before** spawn, as the JSON boolean `true` and the JSON number 1 (types and values are classified identically in Python and SQL, §7.5 item 7; the marker contract is fail-closed, §6.1: an existing `tracked` key that is not the JSON boolean `true`, such as the string "true", is the anomaly `tracked_type`, and the string "1" is not version 1); marks rows the tracked rules may judge and versions the `detail` schema (a row with an unknown version and neither proof nor disposition stays in the normal unresolved set and is not evaluated by a sweeper that does not know the version; a row that carries a proof or disposition under an unknown version is an anomaly, §6.1). It asserts nothing about process state |
| `detail.checkpoint_step_key` | `detail` | the recovery checkpoint of the call (`STEP_TEST` for test calls) so `_park_uncertain` can attach a gate correctly after a crash (§8) |
| `detail.runner_process = {host, pid, create_time}` | `detail` | identity of the Runner process that owns the Job (`capture_identity(os.getpid())`, hostname) so recovery can prove the owner dead (§8) |
| `detail.lifecycle`, `detail.tree`, `detail.termination`, `detail.reason`, `detail.survivors` | `detail` | queryable result; descriptive, never read by a release rule |
| `detail.proof` ∈ `JOB_EMPTY`, `JOB_KILL_ON_CLOSE_ASSUMED`, `NEVER_RAN` | `detail` | the **positive proof** allow-list (§6.1); any other value is an anomaly, never a proof |
| `detail.reason_code` | `detail` | **required whenever a `disposition` is present**, written in the same UPDATE as the disposition and `risk_acceptance` (§7.5 item 7); the only allowed value is the string `OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED` (`DISPOSITION_KIND_RISK_ACCEPTED`); missing, a JSON null, a non-string or any other value is the anomaly kind 5 with the sub-reason `reason_code` (§6.1; the classifier and the SQL predicate validate it identically, §7.4); it is not the `detail.reason` of a command result |
| `detail.disposition = OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED`, `detail.risk_acceptance` | `detail` | the explicit operator exception and its audit record (§7.5); **not** a proof and kept in separate fields; the request itself lives in `process_risk_requests`, never on the row |
| `detail.anomaly_original = {proof, disposition, risk_acceptance, v}` | `detail` | written **only** by the sweeper's anomaly re-judgement (§7.4, orphan sweeper bullet), in the same UPDATE as the positive proof: an exact copy of the invalid `proof`, `disposition`, `risk_acceptance` and `v` that the row carried, so the original anomaly stays in the audit; **no legacy writer and no other B2 writer** writes it; it is a tracked-only key (`TRACKED_ONLY_KEYS`, §6.1), so a row that has it without the `tracked` marker is the anomaly `tracked_missing`; it is never read as a proof or a disposition |
| `detail.anomaly_settlement = {kind, verdict, settled_at, incarnation}` | `detail` | written **only** by that same sweeper write, beside `anomaly_original`: the settlement record of the anomaly (`kind` is the `anomaly_kind` of §6.1, `verdict` the OS verdict that yielded the positive proof, `settled_at`, the Runner `incarnation`); no legacy writer uses it; a tracked-only key; descriptive, never a proof |

`_record_finish` replaces `detail` as a whole today; tracked rows therefore update `detail` by **JSONB merge** (`detail || :new`) so earlier keys survive. OS handles are never persisted: the Job handle lives only in the Runner process.

### 6.1 Settlement record: who writes what

A tracked row is classified in exactly one of the following (revision 12, MA-1). **Normal unresolved** (set U) = `detail.tracked` is the JSON boolean `true` (any other value of an existing `tracked` key is an anomaly, see the marker contract of §6.1, 'Tracked marker and the tracked-only keys') AND `detail.proof` IS NULL AND `detail.disposition` IS NULL (here IS NULL is the null semantics of §7.5 item 7: an absent key and a JSON null both count as no value) — **one predicate, spelled identically** in the shared helper, in every query and in the partial index `ix_executions_tracked_unresolved` of migration `0005`. U holds OPEN_UNPROVEN rows (`finished_at IS NULL`), CLOSED_UNPROVEN rows (`finished_at IS NOT NULL`, an anomaly of a lost write) and rows without a recognised `detail.v` that carry neither proof nor disposition (these block, and no sweeper that does not know the version judges them). **Properly resolved:** RESOLVED_PROVEN = `detail.v = 1`, `finished_at IS NOT NULL`, `detail.proof` ∈ {`JOB_EMPTY`, `JOB_KILL_ON_CLOSE_ASSUMED`, `NEVER_RAN`} and no disposition; RESOLVED_RISK = `detail.v = 1`, `finished_at IS NOT NULL`, no proof, `disposition = OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED`, `detail.reason_code = OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED` and a **valid** `risk_acceptance` (the one schema and validity rule of §7.5 item 7; never a proof, never `tree=EMPTY`). **Anomaly** (set A) = every row that has a tracked marker or a tracked-only key (marker contract of §6.1, 'Tracked marker and the tracked-only keys') and is neither in U nor properly resolved: it carries a proof or a disposition that is not valid, or its `tracked` marker is wrong. Kinds (`anomaly_kind`, computed by one Python classifier whose branches mirror the SQL predicates; **deterministic precedence, the first match wins**): 1. `UNKNOWN_SCHEMA_VERSION` (a proof or a disposition under a `detail.v` that is missing, not a JSON number or a number other than 1: the schema is unsupported, so nothing else about the row is evaluated); 2. `CONTRADICTORY_PROOF_DISPOSITION` (a proof and a disposition together: the combination cannot coexist); 3. `INVALID_PROOF` (a `proof` outside the positive allow-list, or not a string); 4. `INVALID_DISPOSITION_KIND` (a `disposition` other than `OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED`, or not a string); 5. `INCOMPLETE_RISK_ACCEPTANCE` (the disposition kind is valid but `risk_acceptance` fails the validity rule of §7.5 item 7: it is not a JSON object, a required key is missing or a JSON null, a field has the wrong type, format or value (the optional `requested_by` included), its identity does not match its own row, or `detail.reason_code` is missing, a JSON null, not a string or any string other than `OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED`; the first failing check is kept in `anomaly_detail` as the sub-reason `risk_acceptance_not_object`, `key_missing:<key>`, `key_null:<key>`, `type:<key>`, `format:<key>`, `identity:<key>` or `reason_code`, the way kind 6 keeps `finished_at_missing`); 6. `OTHER_SCHEMA_INVALID` (any other required tracked field is missing or malformed, a wrong tracked marker (`tracked_type`, `tracked_missing`) or an undecodable document (`decode_error`), for example a proof or a disposition on a row whose `finished_at` is NULL: the revision-12 `RESOLUTION_WITHOUT_FINISHED_AT`, which is **not** a conflict between a proof and a disposition and is therefore kept as the sub-reason `finished_at_missing` of kind 6 in `anomaly_detail`; the sub-reasons of kind 6 are `decode_error`, `tracked_type`, `tracked_missing`, `finished_at_missing` and `other`, checked in this order). The revision-12 kind names (`RISK_ACCEPTANCE_INCOMPLETE`, `UNKNOWN_DISPOSITION_KIND`, `PROOF_NOT_ALLOWED`, `PROOF_DISPOSITION_CONFLICT`, `RESOLUTION_WITHOUT_FINISHED_AT`) are retired by this revision. The SQL anomaly query decides *membership* of A only; the same precedence exists in SQL as one `CASE` expression, written out in §7.4 (`<ANOMALY_KIND>`), that the diagnostics query and the property test use (Python classifier = SQL `CASE` on every matrix row, §13). **An anomaly is never read as a positive proof, never as a valid disposition and never as normal unresolved:** it has its own query (§7.4) and its own reason code, and every release, acquisition and baseline decision checks U **and** A (the gate path of a valid-link CLEAN project reads neither, §7.5 item 1). *Unresolved* in the rest of this document means U unless the text says "or anomalous". This replaces revision 3's criterion on `detail.tree`, which was undefined for rows that never ran.

| Writer | Situation | `finished_at` | `detail.proof` | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| caller `finally` | `EXITED` / `TERMINATED` | set | `JOB_EMPTY` | `tree=EMPTY` |
| caller `finally` | `SPAWN_FAILED`, cancelled before spawn, `OSError`, `FailClosed` raised before the process existed (`tracked.spawned` false), or killed while suspended and proven gone | set | `NEVER_RAN` | `tree=EMPTY`, `reason` |
| caller `finally` | `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` | **not set** | none | `tree=NOT_EMPTY`/`UNKNOWN`; Job handle retained |
| caller `finally` | result missing and `tracked.spawned` true | **not set** | none | `reason=RESULT_MISSING`; stays unresolved |
| takeover / sweeper | `pid IS NULL` (§8) | set | `NEVER_RAN` | `reason=SUSPENDED_ORPHAN_POSSIBLE` |
| takeover / sweeper | §8 conditions hold | set | `JOB_KILL_ON_CLOSE_ASSUMED` | `termination=ALREADY_EXITED` |
| registry re-check (same Runner process) | Job proven empty, or the recorded settlement result was EMPTY but its write was lost | set | `JOB_EMPTY` | handle or recorded result is in the Runner registry |
| operator risk acceptance (§7.5) | re-verification still unclear | set on an OPEN_UNPROVEN row; an already-set `finished_at`, `outcome`, exit code and termination reason are **never overwritten** | **none** | `disposition=OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED`, `reason_code=OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED`, `risk_acceptance{…}`; `tree` untouched |

Write rules: every closing write is **one UPDATE** that sets `finished_at`, `outcome` and the merged `detail` (including `proof`) together, so `finished_at` and the proof can never disagree. It is **lease-independent**: `WHERE id = :id AND finished_at IS NULL` only, no `leases.verify` (the pattern of `_discard_result`, not of `_record_finish`), so `Runner.stop` — which revokes the lease before cancelling — still closes its rows; and it takes no Task lock. Race with a concurrent terminal transition: the transition either sees the row OPEN_UNPROVEN (forced DIRTY, conservative) or sees it RESOLVED_PROVEN. The sweeper re-judging a CLOSED_UNPROVEN row uses `WHERE id = :id AND detail->>'proof' IS NULL AND detail->>'disposition' IS NULL`; rowcount 0 means somebody settled it meanwhile and the row is re-read. That guard never matches an anomaly (a proof or a disposition is present); anomalies use the anomaly-specific guard of §7.4. **Lock ordering (m6):** any statement that touches several tracked rows (the sweeper, the process-risk worker's result transaction, §7.5) takes the rows in ascending `id` order (`SELECT … ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE`, then update), so both acquire row locks in the same deterministic order, and no OS work happens while a row lock is held (§7.4, §7.5). **Guards by row class (MA-3):** the closing write of the table applies to OPEN_UNPROVEN rows (`WHERE id = :id AND finished_at IS NULL`). Re-judging or accepting risk on a CLOSED_UNPROVEN row uses `WHERE id = :id AND detail->>'proof' IS NULL AND detail->>'disposition' IS NULL` and merges only `proof`, `disposition`, `reason_code` and `risk_acceptance` into `detail`; it never rewrites `finished_at`, `outcome`, the exit code or the earlier termination reason. **A guarded UPDATE that matches 0 rows is never read as success or as proof: the row is always re-read and classified by this ladder, and the first rung that holds wins:** (1) a valid positive proof (allow-listed value, `v = 1`, consistent `finished_at`) → RESOLVED_PROVEN; (2) a valid disposition (its `risk_acceptance` valid by §7.5 item 7) → RESOLVED_RISK, reuse the stored state; (3) neither proof nor disposition → normal unresolved (U); (4) an invalid proof, an invalid disposition (an invalid `risk_acceptance` included) or an unknown schema version → anomaly (A); (5) a contradictory proof-and-disposition combination → anomaly (A) (the kind of every anomaly is chosen by the first-match precedence of the classification rungs of this section, §6.1); (6) rowcount 0 never short-cuts a rung, it only triggers the re-read. The mere presence of a `proof` or `disposition` value is never enough for rung 1 or 2. If the identity (`id`, `pid`, `process_create_time`) changed, stop the current request and re-evaluate.

**Tracked marker and the tracked-only keys (M-1, revision 16; one contract for the whole document).** The classification of a row's `detail` starts with the marker, in this order: (a) `detail` is SQL NULL or not a JSON object: no key exists, a legacy untracked row. *Revision 33, D33-10 (analysis; one handling in SQL and in the Python classifier):* this branch covers a `detail` that is SQL NULL, the JSON null, an array and a scalar, because `jsonb_typeof(detail)` is then SQL NULL, `null`, `array`, `string`, `number` or `boolean` and never `object`, which is exactly the guard of `<TRACKED_ISH>`; such a row is in neither U nor A in SQL and is a legacy untracked row in the classifier (the JSON null of the key `tracked` in (e) is a different case: the value of an existing key of an object). **No independent evidence exists:** by decision H2 there is no column for execution facts, so the marker of a tracked row is only its `detail`; every row that can be identified as tracked (an object `detail` with the key `tracked` or a tracked-only key) is in exactly one of U, `<RESOLVED_VALID>` and A (the partition of the SQL blocks, run in r16 and r18, §13.1; the classifier is not implemented), so **an identifiable tracked row that is unresolved or abnormal is always in U or A** (only a properly resolved row is in neither); the one class outside both is a row that was tracked and whose whole `detail` was later replaced by a non-object, which cannot be told from a legacy row and which could allow CLEAN or `continue`; no B2 writer produces it (they merge keys, H2), and no existing writer produces it either (revision 34, A3, read from the code): the two writers that replace the whole `detail` today write a JSON **object**, never a non-object: `lease_service.py:129-132` (the takeover Txn B: `detail={"abandoned_by_takeover": True}` on every unfinished execution row of the stale run) and `step_runner.py:227-228` (`_record_finish`: `detail={"resumed": …, "termination": …, "permission_requests": …, **result.detail}` on the row that `_record_start` inserted). A row whose `detail` is SQL NULL, the JSON null, an array or a scalar therefore stays a **legacy untracked row in B2**; whether an independent signal or a re-classification is added remains the separate decision O33-1; and a legacy classification is **never proof that a process exited** (such a row is in neither U nor A, and no release, acquisition or baseline rule reads it as evidence). *Which path B2 converts:* only the takeover update of `lease_service.py:129-132`, and only for a **tracked** row that it touches (the OPEN_UNPROVEN row of a tracked test command or of `collect_ids`, §10): it changes from a whole replacement to a JSONB merge (§8; §14, the row of `lease_service.py`), and the merge must preserve the marker and every tracked-only key (`tracked`, `v`, `runner_process`, `checkpoint_step_key`, `proof`, `disposition`, `reason_code`, `risk_acceptance`, `anomaly_original`, `anomaly_settlement`); the merge applies only to a `detail` that is a JSON object (a non-object `detail` is the legacy case above and is not merged into; the behaviour of `||` on a non-object was not run or verified here). `step_runner.py:227-228` writes only rows of untracked agent-CLI executions (§10: provider CLIs stay untracked), has no tracked key to preserve and is not changed by B2. **The existing writers do not already preserve tracked keys** (both replace the whole object, read above), so the conversion is a required change and not an assumption; its tests are the §13 rows 'takeover merge preserves the tracked keys' and 'a non-object `detail` stays legacy' (revision 34). Closing that class would need an independent signal and a re-classification of existing untracked rows (a policy change), so it is **not applied here and is the open decision O33-1 (§12)**; the canonical SQL fence is unchanged. (b) The key `tracked` is absent and no tracked-only key is present: a **legacy untracked row** (every row written before B2 and every untracked agent-CLI row): no anomaly, today's semantics, outside every rule of this document. (c) The key `tracked` is absent but at least one tracked-only key is present: anomaly `OTHER_SCHEMA_INVALID`, sub-reason `tracked_missing`. (d) The key `tracked` is present and its value is the JSON boolean `true`: the tracked-schema classification continues (U, properly resolved or another anomaly kind). (e) The key `tracked` is present and its value is anything else (`false`, the string "true", the number 1, a JSON null, an array, an object): anomaly `OTHER_SCHEMA_INVALID`, sub-reason `tracked_type`. **Fail-closed:** the rows of (c) and (e) are in A, so they are visible in the project-wide unresolved-or-anomalous query and they block CLEAN release (`release_on_terminal`, `_reconcile_once`), new owner acquisition, `accept_baseline` and the PROJECT_DIRTY `continue`; the legacy rows of (a) and (b) get no new anomaly. **The tracked-only key set, defined once:** `TRACKED_ONLY_KEYS` = {`v`, `runner_process`, `checkpoint_step_key`, `proof`, `disposition`, `reason_code`, `risk_acceptance`, `anomaly_original`, `anomaly_settlement`}: exactly the keys that only the B2 tracked writers write (the field table of §6: `v` in the row `detail.tracked = true, detail.v = 1`, `runner_process`, `checkpoint_step_key`, `proof` and `reason_code` each in a row of their own, `disposition` and `risk_acceptance` **together in one row** (two keys of the same `detail` document of the same execution row, written in one UPDATE with `reason_code`; the request itself lives in `process_risk_requests`, never on the row), and `anomaly_original` and `anomaly_settlement` in the two anomaly rows added in revision 22); the SQL predicates, the Python classifier, the anomaly `CASE` and the partial-index predicates are generated from this one constant (the SQL spelling is `jsonb_exists_any(detail, ARRAY[…])`, §7.4). *Why these keys and no others:* a legacy untracked row written by today's code carries only `resumed`, `termination`, `permission_requests` and a provider's `subtype`, `api_error_status` or `reason` (`step_runner.py:212,227-228`; `claude_cli.py:72,86`; `codex_cli.py:108`), `abandoned_by_takeover` (`lease_service.py:132`) or `orchestrator_test_run` with `reason` (`workflow_service.py:780`); therefore `termination` and `reason` are **not** tracked-only (a legacy row with `termination` stays legacy), and the descriptive keys `lifecycle`, `tree`, `survivors` and `reason` are excluded as well because no release rule reads them (§6). A test pins that `TRACKED_ONLY_KEYS` is disjoint from every key that a legacy writer produces; a future writer that wants one of these keys in an untracked row would turn it into an anomaly (fail-closed) and must change the constant and the migration together. **Residual:** a provider's legacy `detail` (`**result.detail`) is open-ended; the pinned test covers today's providers only. **Precedence:** a row whose marker is wrong and that also carries a proof or a disposition under an unknown or absent `v` is kind 1 (the first match wins; kinds 2 to 5 also precede kind 6); the marker defect stays visible in the Python-only `anomaly_detail.marker`. A tracked row without a recognised `detail.v` is in U when it has neither proof nor disposition and an anomaly (`UNKNOWN_SCHEMA_VERSION`) otherwise; it is never read as resolved.

### 6.2 Process-tracking capability (shared with API-only instances)

The Runner process knows whether tracking works on its host; an API-only instance (for example `ALREADY_ACTIVE`, §2 of D) does not. The contract:

- **Value:** `ProcessTrackingCapability{state ∈ SUPPORTED | UNAVAILABLE | UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM | UNKNOWN, reason_code, incarnation_id, lock_backend_pid, checked_at, host, pid}`. `incarnation_id` is a random UUID created when a Runner process acquires the advisory lock; `lock_backend_pid` is the result of `SELECT pg_backend_pid()` executed **on the Runner's advisory-lock connection `_lock_conn` itself**, never on a pool connection. Windows: the self-test of §5.1 step 7 decides `SUPPORTED`/`UNAVAILABLE`; POSIX: `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` (permanent; a POSIX Runner publishes **no** capability row and runs no self-test — the platform is decided locally, see the API boundary of this section). The stored state `UNKNOWN` means "this incarnation has not finished its self-test"; it is not the reader-side `STATUS_UNKNOWN`.
- **Persistence and write order:** a new table `runtime_capabilities(key text PK, value jsonb NOT NULL, updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL)` (`key = 'process_tracking'`), created by migration **`0005`** together with `process_risk_requests` (§7.5) (`down_revision='0004'`, additive; downgrade drops both tables and the three partial indexes; up/down/up and `alembic check` are tests, §13). Windows Runner start (a POSIX Runner skips steps 2–4): (1) acquire the advisory lock; (2) **immediately** upsert `state=UNKNOWN` with the new `incarnation_id`/`lock_backend_pid`, invalidating any earlier incarnation's TTL-fresh value — this upsert is **mandatory**: if it fails the Runner start fails closed (`_settle_failed_start` settles the lock connection and the background tasks, §9.1) and nothing runs with an earlier incarnation's `SUPPORTED` value left behind; (3) run the self-test; (4) upsert the result for the **same** incarnation only (`WHERE value->>'incarnation_id' = :mine`, so a late write of an old incarnation can never overwrite a newer one); (5) only after step (4) was attempted does `start()` continue to the creation of the components and so to the READY and success candidate (SUP-19 step 3). The canonical wording in every place is 'UNKNOWN upsert, self-test, result upsert' (R31-11); a failed result upsert leaves `UNKNOWN` and follows the rule of the 'Refresh task' item of this section. A result of a previous incarnation is never trusted.
- **Refresh task:** the periodic refresh runs in its own bounded asyncio task (`_capability_task`), not inline in `Runner._loop`: every `CAPABILITY_REFRESH_SECONDS`, each write bounded by `CAPABILITY_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; a failed write is logged and retried on the next tick (the TTL then expires into `STATUS_UNKNOWN`). **Stop contract:** `Runner.stop` cancels the task and awaits it within the stop budget (an unfinished task is reported through `RunnerStopIncomplete.components`, §9.1); after stop the advisory lock is released, so readers derive `STATUS_UNKNOWN` without any further write.
- **Trust rule for readers (API, diagnostics, any instance):** the stored value is trusted only if **all** hold: `state != UNKNOWN`; `updated_at` is within `CAPABILITY_TTL_SECONDS` (greater than twice the refresh interval); the Runner advisory lock (`runner_advisory_lock_key`) is currently held by some backend; and that holder (`pg_locks` row with `locktype='advisory'`, `granted`, `database` equal to the OID of the current database, and `pid = lock_backend_pid`) is the one named by the row (so a TTL-fresh row of a dead incarnation is not trusted while a new Runner is still starting). Otherwise the reader state is `STATUS_UNKNOWN`. An instance that holds the live Runner reads its own memory. **`pg_locks` mapping (not verified):** `pg_locks` is cluster-wide while advisory locks are per database, hence the `database` condition. A session advisory lock taken with a 64-bit key is *expected* to appear with `classid = key >> 32`, `objid = key & 0xFFFFFFFF`, `objsubid = 1`. This is PostgreSQL knowledge, not observed in this project and not stated as fact here; a PostgreSQL integration test (§13) takes the lock with the real key and asserts the mapping before the reader rule is relied on. A failing query or a mismatch makes the reader return `STATUS_UNKNOWN` and, on the Runner side, leaves the stored state `UNKNOWN`; a previous incarnation's value is never trusted (fail closed).
- **API boundary (D4/E Test-Run request only; not workflow Tasks, not the existing TESTER step):** evaluated **before any Task row is created**. POSIX `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` → `409 Conflict`, code `PROCESS_TRACKING_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` (**specified by the user**). Windows self-test failure → `409 Conflict`, code `PROCESS_TRACKING_UNAVAILABLE` (code specified by the user, **HTTP status proposed**). Capability not confirmed → code `PROCESS_TRACKING_STATUS_UNKNOWN`, HTTP status **proposed** 503 with `Retry-After`, to be confirmed in the D4 API design (§12 H10 uses the same wording). The three codes are distinct and no Task and no STARTING row is created in any of them. The state is re-read when the Runner starts the Task; if it changed, the Task fails closed (`FAILED`, `PROCESS_TRACKING_UNAVAILABLE`) before any tracked registration. API-only instances read the table through the trust rule of this section and return the same result for Windows. **The permanent POSIX decision is local (n8):** it needs no database row, so a POSIX instance — including an API-only one with no Runner and no row — answers `409 PROCESS_TRACKING_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` from the local OS; `PROCESS_TRACKING_STATUS_UNKNOWN` is used only on a Windows instance whose current-incarnation capability cannot be confirmed. API and Runner are assumed to run on the same OS (a split-OS deployment is not covered, unverified). Workflow Tasks and the existing TESTER step keep the POSIX degrade; only D4/E Test-Run requests are refused, before any Task exists.
- **Diagnostics item `PROCESS_TRACKING`** (`DiagnosticsService` gains an async capability reader, §14) uses the same reason codes in `cause`: `SUPPORTED` → PASS; `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` → WARN, `blocks_execution=false` (workflow Tasks and TESTER steps still run, untracked); `UNAVAILABLE` → FAIL, `blocks_execution=true` (tracked TESTER steps fail closed); `STATUS_UNKNOWN` → UNKNOWN, `blocks_execution=false`. `blocks_features=["TEST_RUN"]` (new optional item field) is present **only for the three non-SUPPORTED states**; a `SUPPORTED` item carries no `blocks_features`.
- **Existing TESTER step:** POSIX → degrade (`detail.tracking="UNTRACKED_PLATFORM"`, no STARTING row); Windows `UNAVAILABLE` → fail closed.

## 7. Tracked commands

### 7.1 Protocol

A *tracked* command is one whose caller passes a `TrackedRun(execution_id, run_key, cancel_scope)`:

1. the caller commits `Execution(outcome=STARTING, role=TESTER, provider=LOCAL, run_id, runner_id, detail.tracked, detail.runner_process, …)` **before** `CommandExecutor.run`, in its own short transaction (no transaction is held while the command runs). **Registration transaction contract** (the row carries `detail.checkpoint_step_key`): lock the Task row (`TaskRepository.lock`), verify the lease (`leases.verify`), require the Task not terminal and `assert_owner` for the project write lock, then insert. Lock order Task → TaskRun, exactly as `StepRunner._record_start`; no new lock edge. Because the Task row lock is also held by every terminal transition (§7.4), **a new tracked execution cannot be registered once a terminal transition has started, and a terminal transition cannot slip past a registration in flight**;
2. the executor runs the §5.1 protocol; `on_started` persists `pid`/`process_create_time` before resume through the **fenced** update of §5.1 step 5;
3. the executor fills `TrackedRun.result` (a `CommandResult`) **before it returns or re-raises** (also when it re-raises `CancelledError`), so the caller can always settle the row;
4. the caller closes the row in a shielded `finally`: `EXITED`/`TERMINATED`/`SPAWN_FAILED` → `finished_at`, `terminated_at`, `outcome`, merged `detail`; `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` → `finished_at` stays NULL (§7.2). The write follows §6.1 (one lease-independent UPDATE with the proof). The executor sets `tracked.spawned = true` right after the process exists; an exception raised before that (for example `resolve_executable`'s `FailClosed`, which happens outside the settlement block) closes the row as `NEVER_RAN` and propagates as today, whereas `result is None` with `spawned` true leaves the row unresolved (`RESULT_MISSING`). A crash before step 4 leaves the row to §8.

Key namespaces (m9): the **scope key** is `f"{run_id}:tracked:{scope_id}"` (one per scope, §9) and a command's `run_key` is `f"{scope_key}:{execution_id}"`. Both start with `run_id`, so `Runner._cancel_cli(run_id)` (Runner stop, lease loss) reaches every live command through the executor's prefix match (`K == P` or `K` starts with `P + ":"`), a cancel of the scope key reaches all commands of the scope, a cancel of one `run_key` reaches only that command, and no key can collide with a step key `{run_id}:{step_id}` used by the tester CLI.

### 7.2 Delivery of `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` and ownership

1. `CommandExecutor` returns `lifecycle=TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` (or settles it before re-raising).
2. `TestPolicyService.run` and `collect_ids` **stop the command sequence** on it, never parse JUnit as a pass, and raise the existing `TerminationUnconfirmed` (`step_runner.py:57`) with the execution id **and a `checkpoint_step_key`** (new optional attribute; `STEP_TEST` for test calls; also written to `detail.checkpoint_step_key` at registration so a crash keeps it); they do not return a "failed test" result. `_park_for_recovery` uses that key when no RUNNING/INTERRUPTED step exists, instead of falling back to `STEP_PLAN` (this matters for `ids_before`, which runs before the tester step begins). An exception raised from inside `evaluate` must leave the tester step RUNNING so the RECOVERY gate attaches to it (to be confirmed by test).
3. The `Execution` row stays open (`finished_at` NULL): `unterminated_executions` returns it, so `_finalize_cancel` and `_recovery_unsafe` (role `TESTER` ∈ `STEP_ROLE.values()`) see it, like an unconfirmed agent CLI.
4. `WorkflowService` handles the error as today: `_park_for_recovery` → RECOVERY gate; the Task is not terminal, so **the project write ownership stays**. There is no automatic retry and no clean release.
5. A later Human Gate **abort** may end the Task but follows §7.4: it does not release the lock as CLEAN. OS work stays out of gate handlers (§8).
6. **Other outcomes of a tracked command:** `CANCELLED` (user cancel, Runner stop, lease loss, cancel during the suspended phase) → `TestPolicyService.run`/`collect_ids` raise `TaskCancelled` after the row is closed, stop the sequence and parse nothing — a cancelled test must not be recorded as a failed test and consume a `workflow_iteration`. `TIMEOUT`/`IDLE` keep today's meaning (failed test result / `None` ids). `SPAWN_FAILED` for **infrastructure reasons** (`JOB_CREATE_FAILED`, `JOB_ASSIGN_FAILED`, `IDENTITY_*`, `RESUME_FAILED`) raises `FailClosed("PROCESS_TRACKING_UNAVAILABLE")` (the same code as the Windows capability state, §6.2) → `_fail` (Task FAILED, no process ran), never a "failed test" that would loop the developer CLI; `OSError` at spawn stays a normal `ERROR` outcome as today; an executable that is not found raises `FailClosed` from `resolve_executable` (before the settlement block, `_fail` with `FAIL_CLOSED`), as today.
7. `collect_ids` before the tester step (`ids_before`) is tracked too and is preceded by `assert_owner`; its `TerminationUnconfirmed` carries `checkpoint_step_key=STEP_TEST`, so a `continue` of that RECOVERY gate re-enters TESTING instead of PLANNING.

### 7.3 Settling an unconfirmed run

- **Same Runner process (no crash):** the retained Job handle is kept in a Runner-local registry `execution_id → handle`. On takeover/recovery (`LeaseService.acquire` for the run) the registry is consulted first: terminate again and poll; `ActiveProcesses == 0` → write `finished_at` with `proof=JOB_EMPTY`. This is the exit from `TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` that does not need a restart. The registry also keeps the in-memory settlement result of a run whose closing write failed (a DB error in the `finally`), so the sweeper can write `JOB_EMPTY` later without a handle; an entry is dropped only after a closing write with a positive proof has committed.
- **After a restart or crash:** §8.

### 7.4 Abort and every terminal transition (decision H7)

A user abort — or any other terminal transition (`FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, rejection, `COMPLETED`) — **does not replace the termination proof.**

- **Unresolved tracked execution** (§6.1): a row of the Task with `detail.tracked` that is in the normal unresolved set U (tracked, no proof, no disposition: OPEN_UNPROVEN or CLOSED_UNPROVEN). Two private **project-wide** repository queries answer the two sets, each taking exactly one argument `project_id`: `TaskRepository.unresolved_tracked_executions_for_project(project_id)` (U, served by `ix_executions_tracked_unresolved`) and `TaskRepository.anomalous_tracked_executions_for_project(project_id)` (A, next bullet), each reading `executions` as the **only** outer `FROM` table and scoping it with `<PROJECT_SCOPE>` (`task_id IN (SELECT id FROM tasks WHERE project_id = :project_id)`, the SQL block of §7.4; **never a `JOIN` of `tasks` and `executions`**, §7.4 'Project-wide query shape'); **no caller uses either directly** (see the common entry point). A separate task-scoped lookup, `TaskRepository.unresolved_for_task(task_id)`, exists for task-local views only (the report, the diagnostics detail of one Task); its name and signature differ on purpose and **no CLEAN decision ever uses it** (architecture test, §13). `detail.tree` plays no part. **Single criterion of the shared helper (m3, revision 12):** a tracked row is *properly resolved* iff it is RESOLVED_PROVEN or RESOLVED_RISK of §6.1 (a **valid** positive proof, or a valid `disposition=OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED` with a valid `risk_acceptance` record (§7.5 item 7): resolution by the operator's explicit acceptance of the risk); with neither it is in U, and a proof or disposition that is not valid is in A. A proof being present never resolves a row by itself. RESOLVED_RISK is never a termination proof and never `tree=EMPTY`. After an acceptance the project stays `DIRTY_UNRESOLVED` and needs the baseline re-acceptance (§7.5), so the helper's verdict on such a row matters only to a later terminal transition of a Task that still owns the lock, which the H9 flow does not produce (the owner Task is already terminal); the baseline re-acceptance gate remains the barrier.
- **Anomaly query (MA-1; one option chosen: a JSONB validation expression with a partial expression index).** A normalized anomaly column was rejected: it would be a new execution-fact column (H2), and the case that must be found is a faulty writer that stored a bad value, so a flag written by the same writers cannot be trusted. The anomaly set is found by **validating `detail` itself**: `CREATE INDEX ix_executions_tracked_anomaly ON executions (task_id) WHERE <ANOMALY>`, and every named block, `<ANOMALY>` included, is spelled out in the SQL block that belongs to this list item (the validity rule of the one `risk_acceptance` schema, §7.5 item 7, is `<RA_VALID>`). The `?&` array of that block is the nine required keys generated from `RISK_ACCEPTANCE_SCHEMA` (§9.3) and never contains the optional `requested_by`, which has its own optional branch. **`IS NOT TRUE`, never `NOT`:** a missing key makes a branch NULL and `NOT NULL` is NULL, which would silently hide the row; a test pins the missing-key case. **Why no row falls between U and A (M-1):** the classes partition the rows. A row without a tracked marker and without a tracked-only key is legacy untracked and in neither index; every other row is in U when `<U>` is TRUE, otherwise properly resolved when `<RESOLVED_VALID>` is TRUE, otherwise in A, because the A predicate is the complement written with `IS NOT TRUE` (a NULL branch counts as 'not'). `<U>` and `<RESOLVED_VALID>` are disjoint (resolved requires a proof or a disposition, U requires neither). A row with a wrong marker (`tracked` false, "true", 1, a JSON null, or only tracked-only keys), an invalid proof, an incomplete disposition or an unknown schema version is therefore in A and **not** in U: never in both and never in neither. The index holds only anomalous rows (normally none); the project-wide query is `<PROJECT_SCOPE>` (its subquery reads `tasks.project_id`, indexed, `tables.py:87-88`) combined with `<ANOMALY>` on `executions` alone, so the partial indexes let the planner avoid scanning every execution row of the project; the cost still depends on the project's Task count (the `tasks.project_id` range) and on the number of index candidates (unresolved or anomalous rows), and the actual plan and its cost are **unverified until PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN` is run**. The predicate text is defined once (one constant used by the model, migration `0005` and the query; a test pins their equality) because the planner uses a partial index only for a query whose predicate is spelled like the index predicate. **Raw SQL predicates (W5).** Migration `0005` creates every partial index of this document with **raw SQL text** (`postgresql_where=text(...)` or `op.execute`, as `uq_approvals_project_dirty_pending` does, `tables.py:307-309`) and writes the JSON keys as SQL **literals**: SQLAlchemy's JSONB `astext` renders the key as a bind parameter, which an index predicate cannot contain, so no index or query of these predicates uses `astext` or a bound key. Predicate implication must also hold under **generic plans** (asyncpg prepares statements, `config.py:13`): an application query repeats the index predicate as a structurally identical literal expression (one shared constant, §7.4 'Single ownership of the SQL text') and only `task_id`, `project_id` or an approval id are parameters. The Python helper's semantics equal the SQL predicate (a comparison test of the result sets, §13). **Verification plan (verified and not-run items are recorded once, §13.1):** what remains is the inspection of the generated migration SQL, `alembic upgrade`, `downgrade`, `alembic check`, the `EXPLAIN` of each query, the prepared-statement / generic-plan condition (`SET plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan`, then `EXPLAIN EXECUTE`), actual index usage (`pg_stat_user_indexes.idx_scan` before and after) and the helper-versus-query result-set comparison; none of these has been run.

The named blocks of this item are the SQL text of the classification. `R` stands for the text `detail -> 'risk_acceptance'`, and each name in angle brackets for a regular-expression literal of §9.3 or for another named block of this list; the migration writes every one of them out as a SQL literal (no bind parameter, no `astext`; every jsonb comparison literal is spelled `'…'::jsonb`). `<RA_VALID>` and `<RESOLVED_VALID>` are **rendered from `RISK_ACCEPTANCE_SCHEMA`** (§7.5 item 7, §9.3) and the key list of `<TRACKED_ISH>` from `TRACKED_ONLY_KEYS` (§6.1); this is the only SQL text of these rules: the anomaly `CASE` (`<ANOMALY_KIND>`, written out once here), the resolved query and the index predicates embed these same blocks. **Single ownership of the SQL text (revision 17):** these blocks are the only definition of the SQL predicate text; other sections refer to them by block name and never restate a fragment. The text is rendered once into named constants (`TRACKED_ISH_SQL`, `U_SQL`, `RA_VALID_SQL`, `RESOLVED_VALID_SQL`, `ANOMALY_SQL`, `ANOMALY_KIND_SQL` and `PROJECT_SCOPE_SQL`; the `pid` comparand `(pid::text)::jsonb` is the canonical SQL fragment `PID_JSONB_SQL`, written literally in `<RA_VALID>`: it has no placeholder and is not rendered separately, purity paragraph of §7.4); migration `0005` freezes the rendered text, and the model's index definitions and the repository queries import the constants; a test compares the frozen migration text, the model text and the query text by string equality instead of relying on hand copies (§13). The `CASE` is evaluated on rows of A only; `<KIND6_SUBREASON>` refines kind 6, and the sub-reasons of kinds 1 to 5 and `decode_error` exist in the Python classifier only. The query blocks at the end of the SQL block (`<PROJECT_SCOPE>`, `<PROJECT_U_QUERY>`, `<PROJECT_A_QUERY>`, `<RISK_PAGE_OWN>`, `<RISK_PAGE_REST>`, `<PROJECT_U_PAGE>`, `<RISK_TARGET_LOCK>`, `<JUDGEABLE>`, `<SWEEP_PAGE>`) keep the named bind parameters `:project_id`, `:task_id`, `:last_seen_id`, `:page_size` and `:target_ids` (a list bind); only the index predicates are literal-only. `:bounded_limit` (the cap + 1 of `LIMIT :bounded_limit`, §7.4 'TrackedBlock, the anomaly item and the bounded diagnostics DTO') is a query-level bind that the entry point appends **outside** the canonical blocks and outside the SQL fence; it is part of no block and is **excluded from the byte-equality comparison** of the frozen migration text, the model text and the query text. **Binds (revision 21, corrected in revision 22).** `:project_id` is a bind that **is** part of the text of the block `<PROJECT_SCOPE>` (it is written inside the block and stays a named bind in every query), and `<PROJECT_SCOPE>` appears in **no** index predicate. The other binds `:task_id`, `:last_seen_id`, `:page_size`, `:target_ids` and `:bounded_limit` belong to no predicate block. The byte-equality test therefore covers (a) the predicate blocks `<U>`, `<RESOLVED_VALID>` and `<ANOMALY>` as they appear in the index predicates (model and migration) and in every query, with no bind inside them, and (b) the block `<PROJECT_SCOPE>`, with its `:project_id` placeholder, as it appears in every query and never in an index predicate; no other bind is part of any compared text. The page limit is reconciled by name: `LIMIT :page_size` is the keyset page size written inside the page blocks `<RISK_PAGE_OWN>`, `<RISK_PAGE_REST>`, `<PROJECT_U_PAGE>` and `<SWEEP_PAGE>`; `LIMIT :bounded_limit` (cap + 1) is a different limit that the entry point appends to the two helper queries `<PROJECT_U_QUERY>` and `<PROJECT_A_QUERY>` only; the two never meet in one statement. The SQL fence differs from revisions 19 and 20 by the two blocks `<PROJECT_U_PAGE>` and `<RISK_TARGET_LOCK>` (added in revision 21) and from revision 21 by the rewritten `<RISK_TARGET_LOCK>` (revision 22: one ordered statement with the list bind `:target_ids`); the English and the Korean fence are byte-identical to each other (a parity check, §13).

```sql
-- <TRACKED_ISH>   (a row with a tracked marker or a tracked-only key; TRACKED_ONLY_KEYS is one constant, section 6.1)
jsonb_typeof(detail) = 'object'
AND ( jsonb_exists(detail, 'tracked')
      OR jsonb_exists_any(detail, ARRAY['v','runner_process','checkpoint_step_key','proof','disposition','reason_code','risk_acceptance','anomaly_original','anomaly_settlement']) )

-- <U>   (normal unresolved; the predicate of ix_executions_tracked_unresolved)
(detail -> 'tracked') = 'true'::jsonb
AND (detail ->> 'proof') IS NULL AND (detail ->> 'disposition') IS NULL

-- <RA_VALID>   (the validity rule of risk_acceptance; R = detail -> 'risk_acceptance')
jsonb_typeof(detail -> 'reason_code') = 'string' AND (detail ->> 'reason_code') = 'OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED'
AND jsonb_typeof(detail -> 'risk_acceptance') = 'object'
AND (detail -> 'risk_acceptance') ?& ARRAY['approval_id','execution_id','pid','create_time','last_verdict','requested_at','rationale','reverify_result','applied_at']
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'approval_id')  = 'string' AND (R ->> 'approval_id')  ~ <UUID_RE>
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'execution_id') = 'string' AND (R ->> 'execution_id') ~ <UUID_RE> AND (R ->> 'execution_id') = id::text
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'pid')          = 'number' AND (R -> 'pid') = (pid::text)::jsonb AND pid BETWEEN 1 AND 2147483647
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'create_time')  = 'number' AND (R -> 'create_time') >= '0'::jsonb
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'last_verdict') = 'string' AND (R ->> 'last_verdict') = 'UNCLEAR'
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'requested_at') = 'string' AND (R ->> 'requested_at') ~ <TS_RE>
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'rationale')    = 'string' AND char_length(R ->> 'rationale') BETWEEN 1 AND 2000
    AND (R ->> 'rationale') ~ '[^ \t\n]' AND (R ->> 'rationale') !~ <RATIONALE_FORBIDDEN>
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'reverify_result') = 'string'
    AND (R ->> 'reverify_result') IN ('UNKNOWN','ACCESS_DENIED','OTHER_HOST','H3_DISABLED','IDENTITY_RECORD_MISSING')
AND jsonb_typeof(R -> 'applied_at')   = 'string' AND (R ->> 'applied_at')   ~ <TS_RE>
AND ( NOT ((detail -> 'risk_acceptance') ? 'requested_by')
      OR ( jsonb_typeof(R -> 'requested_by') = 'string' AND (R ->> 'requested_by') ~ <REQUESTED_BY_RE> ) )

-- <RESOLVED_VALID>   (properly resolved: RESOLVED_PROVEN or RESOLVED_RISK)
(detail -> 'tracked') = 'true'::jsonb
AND jsonb_typeof(detail -> 'v') = 'number' AND (detail -> 'v') = '1'::jsonb
AND finished_at IS NOT NULL
AND (
  ( (detail ->> 'proof') IN ('JOB_EMPTY','JOB_KILL_ON_CLOSE_ASSUMED','NEVER_RAN')
    AND (detail ->> 'disposition') IS NULL )
  OR
  ( (detail ->> 'proof') IS NULL
    AND (detail ->> 'disposition') = 'OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED'
    AND <RA_VALID> )
)

-- <ANOMALY>   (membership of A; the predicate of ix_executions_tracked_anomaly)
(<TRACKED_ISH>) AND ((<U>) IS NOT TRUE) AND ((<RESOLVED_VALID>) IS NOT TRUE)

-- <ANOMALY_KIND>   (evaluated on rows of A; the first matching WHEN wins)
CASE
  WHEN ((detail ->> 'proof') IS NOT NULL OR (detail ->> 'disposition') IS NOT NULL)
       AND (jsonb_typeof(detail -> 'v') = 'number' AND (detail -> 'v') = '1'::jsonb) IS NOT TRUE
    THEN 'UNKNOWN_SCHEMA_VERSION'
  WHEN (detail ->> 'proof') IS NOT NULL AND (detail ->> 'disposition') IS NOT NULL
    THEN 'CONTRADICTORY_PROOF_DISPOSITION'
  WHEN (detail ->> 'proof') IS NOT NULL
       AND (jsonb_typeof(detail -> 'proof') = 'string'
            AND (detail ->> 'proof') IN ('JOB_EMPTY','JOB_KILL_ON_CLOSE_ASSUMED','NEVER_RAN')) IS NOT TRUE
    THEN 'INVALID_PROOF'
  WHEN (detail ->> 'disposition') IS NOT NULL
       AND (jsonb_typeof(detail -> 'disposition') = 'string'
            AND (detail ->> 'disposition') = 'OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED') IS NOT TRUE
    THEN 'INVALID_DISPOSITION_KIND'
  WHEN (detail ->> 'disposition') = 'OPERATOR_RISK_ACCEPTED' AND (<RA_VALID>) IS NOT TRUE
    THEN 'INCOMPLETE_RISK_ACCEPTANCE'
  ELSE 'OTHER_SCHEMA_INVALID'
END

-- <KIND6_SUBREASON>   (refines the ELSE branch; the Python-only decode_error is checked before these)
CASE
  WHEN jsonb_exists(detail, 'tracked') AND ((detail -> 'tracked') = 'true'::jsonb) IS NOT TRUE THEN 'tracked_type'
  WHEN NOT jsonb_exists(detail, 'tracked') THEN 'tracked_missing'
  WHEN finished_at IS NULL AND ((detail ->> 'proof') IS NOT NULL OR (detail ->> 'disposition') IS NOT NULL) THEN 'finished_at_missing'
  ELSE 'other'
END

-- <PROJECT_SCOPE>   (every project-wide query: executions is the ONLY outer FROM table; never JOIN tasks and executions)
task_id IN (SELECT id FROM tasks WHERE project_id = :project_id)

-- <PROJECT_U_QUERY>   (set U of one project)
SELECT id, task_id, pid, process_create_time, finished_at, detail::text
FROM executions
WHERE <PROJECT_SCOPE> AND (<U>)
ORDER BY id

-- <PROJECT_A_QUERY>   (membership of A of one project; Python then classifies every returned row)
SELECT id, task_id, pid, process_create_time, finished_at, detail::text
FROM executions
WHERE <PROJECT_SCOPE> AND (<ANOMALY>)
ORDER BY id

-- <RISK_PAGE_OWN>   (risk_batch_targets, phase 1: the resumed Task's own U rows; the first page has no AND id > :last_seen_id)
SELECT id, task_id, pid, process_create_time, finished_at, detail::text
FROM executions
WHERE <PROJECT_SCOPE> AND task_id = :task_id AND (<U>) AND id > :last_seen_id
ORDER BY id
LIMIT :page_size

-- <RISK_PAGE_REST>   (phase 2: the other Tasks of the project; the first page has no AND id > :last_seen_id)
SELECT id, task_id, pid, process_create_time, finished_at, detail::text
FROM executions
WHERE <PROJECT_SCOPE> AND task_id <> :task_id AND (<U>) AND id > :last_seen_id
ORDER BY id
LIMIT :page_size

-- <PROJECT_U_PAGE>   (project-wide U keyset page: continue discovery, project diagnostics discovery and every other project-level consumer without a resumed Task; one ascending id stream, no OWN/REST split; the first page has no AND id > :last_seen_id)
SELECT id, task_id, pid, process_create_time, finished_at, detail::text
FROM executions
WHERE <PROJECT_SCOPE> AND (<U>) AND id > :last_seen_id
ORDER BY id
LIMIT :page_size

-- <RISK_TARGET_LOCK>   (CM-4, revision 22: the final risk snapshot, locked in the decision transaction by ONE ordered statement; :target_ids is the whole candidate set in any order; the rows still in U come back and are locked in ascending id; 0 rows = nothing is left)
SELECT id, task_id, pid, process_create_time, finished_at, detail::text
FROM executions
WHERE <PROJECT_SCOPE> AND (<U>) AND id = ANY(:target_ids)
ORDER BY id
FOR UPDATE

-- <JUDGEABLE>   (W3: the owning Task is terminal or the run is not live; EXISTS subqueries only, never a JOIN)
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks t WHERE t.id = executions.task_id AND t.status IN ('COMPLETED','FAILED','CANCELLED'))
OR run_id IS NULL
OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM task_runs r WHERE r.id = executions.run_id
           AND (r.status IN ('FINISHED','ABANDONED') OR (r.status = 'RUNNING' AND r.lease_expires_at <= now())))

-- <SWEEP_PAGE>   (orphan sweeper, all projects: judgeable U rows and all A rows in one ascending id stream; the first page has no AND id > :last_seen_id)
SELECT id, task_id, pid, process_create_time, finished_at, detail::text
FROM executions
WHERE ( ((<U>) AND (<JUDGEABLE>)) OR (<ANOMALY>) ) AND id > :last_seen_id
ORDER BY id
LIMIT :page_size
```
