| `DiagnosticCauseOut` | API model, `app/schemas/api.py` | `reason_code`, `severity`, `blocks_execution`, `cause`, `recommendation`, `related_execution_ids`, `related_request_ids` (the fields of §14.1; the cause `TRACKED_EXECUTION_ANOMALY` also carries `anomalies`, `anomalies_returned`, `anomalies_truncated`, `anomalies_total`, `anomalies_total_is_exact` and `may_be_permanently_stuck`) plus `sweeper` (`SweeperStallOut` or `None`), `config_invalid` (`SweeperConfigInvalidOut` or `None`) and `components` (a list of `BackgroundComponentOut`, `[]` by default) | `DiagnosticItemOut.causes` (a list, `[]` by default) | converted by the `response_model` of `app/routers/projects.py` with `from_attributes` (the names are equal); the key `causes` is additive, so the exact key set asserted by `tests/api/test_diagnostics_api.py:70` is updated and never loosened |

The exact-equality assertions that these additions break are **updated in the same change**: `tests/unit/test_runtime_status.py:12-13` (`test_a_running_runner_with_a_clean_recovery_is_ready`: the `as_dict()` equality; the `runner` object gains the keys that SUP-6 and §14.2 add), `tests/api/test_diagnostics_api.py:70` (`test_diagnostics_report_items_with_codes_status_time_cause_and_the_blocking_flag`: the exact item key set `{code, status, checked_at, cause, recommendation, blocks_execution}` gains `causes`, §14.1) and `:112` (`test_health_keeps_its_original_keys_and_adds_readiness`: the `body["runner"]` equality gains `background_degraded` and `sweeper`, §14.2), and `tests/api/test_reports_api.py:116` (`test_the_report_of_a_completed_task_is_built_from_stored_facts_and_not_called_acceptance`) and `:225` (`test_a_waiting_request_is_explained_by_the_runtime_provider_when_one_is_wired`): the `report["runtime"]` equality gains the report runtime keys (`RuntimeOut`, §14.2). The exact-key verification **stays in the test plan**: each updated test compares the **complete** new key set with equality and is never weakened to a subset check; `tests/unit/test_response_contract.py:177` is a fixture and needs no edit (the new report fields have defaults). A test compares the key set of the `/health` `runner.sweeper` object with `SweeperStatusOut`, and the API models have no field for SQL text, `detail`, an exception string, a rationale or a native session id.

**Ownership of the state and the objects (revision 28; exact locations, no field counts).** Runner component state: the registry and the supervisor of `app/services/background_supervisor.py`, one instance owned by `Runner` in `app/services/runner.py`. The runtime snapshot internal dataclasses: `RuntimeSnapshot`, `BackgroundComponentStatus` and the input bundle `RunnerRuntimeState` in `app/services/runtime_status.py`. The diagnostics internal view model: the frozen dataclasses `SweeperStallSnapshot` and `SweeperConfigInvalidSnapshot` of `app/services/sweeper_stall.py` and `BackgroundComponentStatus`, carried by the frozen `DiagnosticCause` of `app/services/diagnostics_service.py`; their attribute names equal the field names of the DTOs. The report dictionary: `ReportService._runtime()` (`report_service.py:325-329`), a plain `dict`, validated by `RuntimeOut` in `finalize` (`app/schemas/reports.py`). The health API schema: no `response_model` (`app/main.py:103-107`); the body is `RuntimeSnapshot.as_dict()` and a test compares its `runner.sweeper` key set with `SweeperStatusOut`. The diagnostics API schema: `DiagnosticCauseOut` with `SweeperStallOut`, `SweeperConfigInvalidOut` and `BackgroundComponentOut`, all in `app/schemas/api.py`, converted by `response_model` in `app/routers/projects.py` (`read_project_diagnostics`). `SweeperStallOut` and `SweeperConfigInvalidOut`: `app/schemas/api.py`. `SweeperStallOut` and `SweeperConfigInvalidOut` are never built by a service. `SweeperStatusOut` and `RuntimeOut`: `app/schemas/reports.py` (`RuntimeOut`, `:202`). `background_degraded`: the source is the Runner property `Runner.background_degraded`, carried by `RuntimeSnapshot.background_degraded`, exposed as `runner.background_degraded` by `as_dict()` and as `RuntimeOut.background_degraded` in the report; the diagnostics carry the component detail list instead.

**Output model of the sweeper status (revision 28; one model, replacing the r27 sentences 'only when stalled' and 'reset when the Runner restarts').** The sweeper status object exists when a stall **or** a configuration-invalid state exists, and always in `/health` and the report as the default object. `stalled` is a boolean; the stall-only fields (`stalled_since`, the cursors, `consecutive_failures`, `last_failure_*`, `next_retry_at`) have explicit defaults (`false`, `null`, 0); the configuration-invalid detail is a separate nested object (`SweeperConfigInvalidOut`) and both can coexist. **Configuration-invalid state without a stall record (CI-only):** the default `SweeperStallOut` (`stalled` false, `consecutive_failures` 0, every other field `null`), the configuration-invalid detail present, the warning `SWEEPER_CONFIG_INVALID` immediate in `/health.warnings`, the report and the diagnostics, and **no** stall-threshold blocker (`ready` and `blockers` are unchanged by it). **Four situations are distinguished:** (1) the configuration is currently valid and no state is active (`config_invalid_active` false); (2) the state is active and the configuration is currently invalid (`config_currently_valid` false); (3) the state is active but the configuration is valid again and the trigger position is not yet passed (`config_currently_valid` true and `clearance_pending` true): the text and the API must **not** claim that the configuration is currently invalid and say that the warning stays until the sweeper passes the recorded position; (4) a stall now (`stalled` true) or an ordinary last failure (`last_failure_*` of a failure that is not the configuration guard). `config_currently_valid` is the result of the latest evaluation of the guard (the entry of a pass, `_recheck_sweeper_configuration` or `start()`; SUP-28, SUP-29) and is `null` before any evaluation of the generation; `next_recheck_at` is the effective time of the next evaluation (the end of the debounce while a wake-up is pending, otherwise the end of the pass wait; `null` when no sweeper task runs) and `next_retry_at` stays the audit value.

**Runtime-status input contract (revision 28).** `runtime_snapshot(lifecycle, startup_outcome, recovery_unsettled, state=None)` gains one fourth parameter with the default `None` ('no background state'), so the callers of today keep working unchanged: `runtime_snapshot(L.RUNNING, S.STARTED, recovery_unsettled=False)` (`tests/unit/test_runtime_status.py:10`) and the positional `runtime_snapshot(L.STOPPED, S.PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED, False)` (`tests/api/test_reports_api.py:218`, `tests/unit/test_diagnostics_service.py:71`). The parameter is one internal frozen dataclass, `RunnerRuntimeState` in `app/services/runtime_status.py` (it imports nothing from `app/schemas`), that bundles the lifecycle, `runner_active`, the sweeper stall snapshot, the configuration-invalid snapshot, the background degraded flag, the degraded component detail and the supervisor state; the first argument `lifecycle` stays the authority for `runner_active` and `ready`, and a differing `lifecycle` inside the bundle is ignored. `snapshot_of(runner, startup_outcome)` builds the bundle duck-typed from these read-only Runner properties: `lifecycle` (existing), `recovery_unsettled` (existing), `sweeper_stall`, `sweeper_config_invalid`, `background_degraded`, `background_components` and `supervisor_state` (a Runner without one of them is read with a default, as `recovery_unsettled` is today). **What changes:** `blockers` gains `SUPERVISOR_DEGRADED` (appended after the lifecycle blocker and `RECOVERY_UNSETTLED`) when the lifecycle is `RUNNING` and the supervisor state is DEGRADED; `ready` (= active and no blocker) becomes false; `runner_active` stays true. **What does not change:** every other combination, and a degraded component other than the supervisor changes none of `ready`, `runner_active` and `blockers`. `RunnerBlocker` is `runtime_status.py:25-33` today and gains one value. **Revision 29:** the bundle also carries `background_revision` (the Runner's read-only property, §14.3).

**`RunnerStopIncomplete` (revision 28; today `__init__(run_ids, recovery=None)`, `runner.py:50-61`; superseded in r29 by SUP-24).** The existing arguments stay compatible; the new optional argument `components` (a tuple of canonical component ids, SUP-24; r28 said 'with their states', superseded in r29) is added, `run_ids` may be an empty tuple and the meaning of `recovery` is unchanged. The message composes the run part, the recovery part and the component part separately; a component-only example is `run_ids = ()` with `components = ('supervisor', 'sweeper:restart-waiter')`. The exception is **never** constructed for an empty failure set, and a `stop()` on a `STOPPED` Runner or on an IDLE unit is an idempotent success without an error (SUP-T T11, T31).

Production code is **not** modified by this document; regression tests for every row are listed in §13. **Approval boundary (proposed; nothing is approved):** tracking on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is not approved; POSIX real-execution verification has not been done; root process exit detected first by `returncode`; as a result the normal-exit outcome of untracked commands can differ from today's TIMEOUT or ALREADY_EXITED.

Not run until approval and implementation: every test and check of this document (this document changes no tests). **Limitations:** `JOB_CLOSE_SETTLE_SECONDS = 2.0` is an unverified design default (1.5 s was the only observation, in a limited probe; other Windows environments are unverified); the other new timing defaults of §9.2, the PostgreSQL items that §13.1 lists as not run (migration up/down/check, every `EXPLAIN` and generic plan, actual index use, the unique lineage index flow, the `pg_locks` mapping, the classifier-versus-SQL equivalence), the Windows Job Object behaviour beyond §2.1 and every POSIX, Gradle and Maven behaviour were not run and are **not claimed**. **Approval boundary (proposed; nothing is approved):** tracking on Windows only; the untracked settlement hardening and the POSIX degrade and refusal contract are in scope; POSIX process tracking is not approved; POSIX real-execution verification has not been done; root process exit detected first by `returncode`; as a result the normal-exit outcome of untracked commands can differ from today's TIMEOUT or ALREADY_EXITED.

### 14.3 Diagnostics cache key and the background revision (revision 29, decision D29-5)

**Real code today:** `DiagnosticsService.diagnose` builds its cache key from the project identity, the workspace path, the hash of the test policy, `DIAGNOSTICS_POLICY_VERSION` (`policies.py:169`, value 1), `runtime.ready`, `runtime.blockers`, the write-lock owner and the workspace state (`diagnostics_service.py:111-113`), with a TTL of `DIAGNOSTICS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` = 30.0 (`policies.py:172`); the supervisor DEGRADED state, the configuration-invalid state and the stall state are in none of these, so a change of them would stay invisible for up to 30 s. **The contract:** (1) `DIAGNOSTICS_POLICY_VERSION` is bumped (to 2) in the implementation plan, because the set of causes changes; (2) the Runner owns a **background-state revision**, a non-negative `int` (`Runner._background_revision`, exposed through the read-only property `background_revision`); (3) **who increments it:** the `Runner` method that the supervisor and the done-callbacks call synchronously (no `await`, so the increment is atomic on the one event loop), only when a value **really changes**: the active toggles (configuration-invalid, stall), the component state, the consecutive failures, the failure position, the last failure code, the next retry time, whether the configuration is currently valid, the clearance pending, the stall count and state, the supervisor DEGRADED state, the exhausted restart budget, the activation and the clearance of the configuration-invalid state, and any published component detail (`reason_code`, `since`, `restart_exhausted`); the evaluation timestamps `config_evaluated_at` and `next_recheck_at` never bump it (they change on every evaluation and would defeat the cache; they are informational, decide no state and are not part of the key, so a cached item may show them up to one TTL old; this concerns only these two timestamps and **never** a derived display value or any other state, which the key below covers; revision 35, D35-1); the stall and configuration-invalid records that the sweeper task writes call the same synchronous bump method (revision 32, W6); an identical rewrite never bumps it; it is never incremented by a tick, a read or an unchanged re-evaluation, and it never decreases or resets inside one Runner object (a new process starts again at 0, which is safe because the cache lives in the process); (4) **how it reaches diagnostics:** `snapshot_of` reads the property into the bundle `RunnerRuntimeState` (§14.2), `RuntimeSnapshot` gains the field `background_revision: int` (default 0; **not** part of `as_dict()` and therefore not in `/health`), and the cache key is **the diagnostics policy version, the background revision (or a fingerprint of it) and the existing ready and blocker inputs** (`runtime.ready`, `runtime.blockers`, the write-lock owner, the workspace state, the workspace identity and the hash of the test policy) **and the derived-state set** (revision 35, D35-1: the sorted tuple of `(unit, display_state)` of every derived value of table SUP-DS, computed from the **same** registry snapshot as the other runtime inputs of that read and not from a second read; a derived value is a lookup that writes nothing, so it never increments the background revision and only this set makes its change visible); (5) an unchanged state keeps the key, so there is no needless miss, and a change is visible at the next read, a derived value that appears or disappears inside the TTL included (case A and case B of SUP-17); the 30 s TTL stays for every input that neither the key nor the revision covers (for example the database facts that diagnostics items read). **Output notes:** `DiagnosticCause` does not exist in code today (`diagnostics_service.py` has `Status`, `DiagnosticItem` and `DiagnosticsReport` only); the causes of §14.1 are new internal frozen dataclasses of `diagnostics_service.py`, mapped explicitly to the API type `DiagnosticCauseOut` (`from_attributes` only where the names are equal); `DiagnosticItemOut.causes` is an additive field with an empty list as default, so it adds the key `causes` to the exact key set that `tests/api/test_diagnostics_api.py:70` asserts, which is **updated, not loosened** (§13). The field list of the internal cause type is canonical in the field plan of this section; the revision-29 statement that it was not made canonical is superseded in r30.
